first.rationale: The most urgent threat is a competitor's aggressive entry pricing actively poaching price-sensitive SMB accounts, which directly implicates memory_73 (promotional pricing effective for price-sensitive SMB, held across billing plans, cut time-to-value). This is a closer match to the current threat than the activation/onboarding declines, which are milder (4-6%) and already have two supporting but possibly redundant memories (memory_31, memory_86). I want to verify memory_73's original record to confirm the 'revenue lift' reflected durable, qualified revenue rather than short-term discount-driven volume that could erode long-term margins or attract low-loyalty customers — this matters because the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not just acquisition. I also verify memory_31 to check whether the SMB activation lift from field-cutting was measured on a comparable population and time horizon, since it competes for the same experiment slot and touches the same SMB segment under pressure. Given only one experiment slot and competing plausible responses, I'm running promotional_pricing as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout, since race-to-the-bottom pricing dynamics could undermine long-term revenue quality even if it stems short-term SMB churn to the competitor. This preserves optionality to pivot to onboarding/activation fixes next cycle if the guarded pricing test shows weak downstream retention or margin signals.
